I confirmed the writer's flag. The ATO rate is $1 per load for work-only clothing and 50c per load when other laundry is included. Claims under $150 need no written evidence only when total work-related expenses are $300 or less. No constant holds these values.
constants: No constant holds this. It should live in lib/constants/tax-return-2025-26.ts (for example laundryPerLoadWorkOnly, laundryPerLoadMixed, laundryNoEvidenceCap) and be rendered from there.

claims: For employees with HECS-HELP debt, deductions can also reduce your compulsory repayment amount by lowering your repayment income below a threshold.
Deductions can reduce your compulsory HELP repayment 'by lowering your repayment income below a threshold'.
whys: The site's own helpRepayment2025_26 (lib/constants/tax-return-2025-26.ts line 158, using HECS_HELP_2025_26 in lib/constants/australian-tax.ts line 476) uses the new marginal system, where repayments are charged on income above the threshold. Under that system any deduction above the threshold lowers the repayment. It does not need to push income below a threshold, so the sentence describes the old whole-of-income system.

I confirmed the writer's flag against HECS_HELP_2025_26 (lib/constants/australian-tax.ts:476). It uses marginal bands (15c per $1 over $67,000, $8,700 + 17c over $125,000), so any deduction that lowers repayment income above $67,000 lowers the repayment. The sentence describes the old whole-of-income system. There is also an inconsistency inside the constant: its top band (179,286+) charges 10% of total repayment income, which also needs checking against the ATO 2025-26 HELP schedule.

The 47% no-TFN rate is triggered by not quoting a TFN, not by a declaration being filled in wrongly. For foreign residents the no-TFN rate is 45%. The bold text is protected, so I left it as it is.
constants: lib/constants/australian-tax.ts (top marginal rate + Medicare levy). 47%, 45% and 2% are hard-coded at lines 62, 82, 158, 180 and 215.
reviewerNotes: I agree with all five of the writer's factQuestions. (1) 47% is called the 'highest marginal rate' (line 62), but line 215 says it is 45% + 2% Medicare. (2) The 28 days applies only after you tick 'I have made a separate application', not to the declaration itself (lines 65, 80, 82, 180). (3) For changes with the same payer the ATO uses a withholding declaration (NAT 3093), not a new TFN declaration. Line 127 already says so, but lines 149, 154, 164, 169, 189, 193 and 194 do not. (4) The employer-group wording at line 192 is too broad. (5) 'likely already claiming' for Centrelink payees at line 111. I made no text changes for them because the claims sit in locked or protected strings.

claims: You must provide it within 28 days of starting work.
whys: The ATO's 28-day window is for quoting your TFN after you tick 'I have made a separate application'. The employer's deadline is 14 days: if it has no declaration by then, it lodges one with the details it has. This sentence applies the 28 days to the whole declaration. Line 180 ('If you don't provide your TFN within 28 days') also suggests the 47% rate starts only after 28 days, even when you have made no TFN application.
constants: none (prose). An ATO deadline constant would help.

claims: Submit a new TFN declaration when you take on or pay off a HECS debt, change your tax-free threshold claim or change residency (also the table 'How to Fix' cells at lines 149, 154, 164 and 169).
whys: For changes with the same payer the ATO uses a withholding declaration (NAT 3093), not a new TFN declaration. Line 127 on the same page already says to give a 'withholding declaration' once the debt is repaid, so the page contradicts itself. Table cells and headings are locked.

claims: Starting a new job: required for every new job, even if you have worked for the same employer group before.
whys: Check the ATO rule for a payee who rejoins the same payer. Within an employer group, separate legal entities need their own declaration, but the line is broader than that.

claims: Your employer can withhold at normal rates for 28 days while you wait. After 28 days without a TFN, the 47% rate applies.
whys: This repeats the 28-day issue in the callout box. Under the ATO rule, the 47% (or 45% for foreign residents) rate applies straight away if you neither quote a TFN nor claim an exemption or separate application. The page currently suggests that everyone gets a 28-day grace period.

claims: If you receive a taxable payment such as JobSeeker, Youth Allowance or Austudy, you are likely already claiming the threshold from that payment.
whys: This is a population hedge with no source. It should state the ATO rule for Centrelink payees (whether the threshold is claimed from the payment) without 'likely'. I left it because changing it would mean stating a rule the page does not cite.

claims: Claim the tax-free threshold at your main job only (usually the highest-paying one).
whys: 'usually' is an unsourced hedge on a tax rule. The ATO says to claim the threshold from the payer who usually pays the highest salary or wage. Consider wording that follows the ATO's instead of a population hedge.

claims: Above it you pay 15c for each dollar up to $45,000
It's a zero-rate band that every resident gets once per income year

Scope is too wide: the same page (line 181) says part-year residents get a reduced, pro-rated threshold, not the full {T} band. Could read 'every full-year resident'. Left unchanged because it narrows a factual claim.

claims: No. Your employer does not factor it into PAYG withholding. (The guide body says the same at modules/guide/zone-tax-offset.tsx:129.)

whys: The ATO Withholding declaration (NAT 3093) lets an employee ask the employer to reduce withholding for a zone, overseas forces or invalid carer tax offset. I agree with the writer. The ATO Withholding declaration (NAT 3093) has carried a question that lets an employee claim a zone, overseas forces or invalid and invalid carer tax offset through reduced withholding. claims: You always keep more of a pay rise than you lose in tax.
whys: The Medicare levy surcharge applies to the whole income once it crosses a tier (calculateMLS uses income * rate). A single person without private hospital cover who goes from just under to just over the tier 1 threshold pays about 1% of their whole income in surcharge, which can be more than the rise itself. The sentence is only true for the income tax brackets on their own. It also uses 'always', a word the brand voice forbids in tax advice. I left the text as it is: the sentence needs to be limited to income tax brackets, or to name the surcharge exception.
reviewerNotes: The writer's fact question is confirmed. calculateMLS (lib/constants/australian-tax.ts:705-708) returns income * tier rate on the whole income. A single person without private hospital cover who crosses the tier 1 minimum by a small rise pays roughly 1% of their whole income, which is more than the rise. So 'You always keep more of a pay rise than you lose in tax' is false in that case, and it also uses the forbidden word 'always' in tax advice. The brief says not to change facts, so I left the sentence. It needs an owner decision: limit it to the income tax brackets, or name the surcharge exception.

claims: "The same Act adds a new offset on top of the rate cut. The Working Australians Tax Offset pays $250 against tax from 2027-28"
whys: Here "the same Act" means LEGISLATED_CUT_2027_28.act, the Treasury Laws Amendment (More Cost of Living Relief) Act 2025. But lib/constants/tax-2027-28.ts (lines 15-27, 58) says the WATO comes from the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026, assented 26 June 2026. The ATO also describes the WATO as a non-refundable maximum benefit of $250, so "pays $250" overstates it. It should say "up to $250", and only when tax payable is above $250.
constants: WATO.maxOffset, WATO.royalAssent and WATO.firstIncomeYear in lib/constants/tax-2027-28.ts (the $250 is typed into the JSX, not rendered from the constant)
reviewerNotes: I confirmed the writer's question. Source line 424 says "The same Act adds a new offset", which means LEGISLATED_CUT_2027_28.act. But lib/constants/tax-2027-28.ts (lines 15-27, 58-59) credits the WATO to the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026, assented 26 June 2026. The text also has "$250" typed in and says "pays $250", while the ATO describes a non-refundable maximum benefit of $250. This needs a source fix that uses WATO.maxOffset, and the wording should be "up to".

claims: Working holiday makers (417 and 462 visas) and non-residents ... their take-home pay is lower at the same salary.
Australian resident tax rates ... apply to most migrants who ... are residents for tax purposes.
whys: Working holiday makers pay 15% from the first dollar up to $45,000 and then the resident rates, but as non-residents they pay no Medicare levy (2%). The extra tax compared with a resident is about $2,730 plus LITO, so above roughly $136,500 a working holiday maker's take-home pay can be HIGHER than a resident's. The sentence is not true at every salary. Check it against the engine's WHM and non-resident modes.

Working holiday makers who are residents for tax purposes are still taxed at the WHM rates. The answer would be more precise if it named that exception instead of relying on 'most'. That needs a content decision, so the wording was not changed in this pass.
reviewerNotes: The writer's WHM question holds up. WHM is 15% from $0 to $45,000 and resident is 0% up to $18,200, then 15%, so the WHM pays about $2,730 more plus the LITO they don't get. But a WHM pays no 2% Medicare levy. Above roughly $136,500, a WHM takes home more than a resident. Non-residents (30% from the first dollar, no Medicare levy) cross over too, at about $474,000. So 'their take-home pay is lower at the same salary' is not true at every salary. Left for the owner to check against the engine.

claims: Under most awards Saturday work pays around {saturdayMin} to {saturdayMax} of the base rate ... penalty rates apply ... typically weekends, public holidays, overtime and late nights.

reviewerNotes: I confirmed the writer's factQuestions are valid and left the text unchanged per the rules. The 'shaded Medicare levy' claim at $52,254.80 is wrong because the full 2% applies. The Wednesday pay-cycle example fails because 1 July 2026 is a Wednesday. The population claims and the $450m costing also remain on the writer's list.

TBC: 'links directly' to the concessional and non-concessional caps overstates the link. TBC: the 13 July 2026 display date is in stale future tense. I left all of them unchanged, as the brief requires.

claims: The $2 minimum donation threshold for deductible gift recipients has been removed, backdated to gifts made from 1 July 2024

Please confirm against the ATO gifts and donations page. If it is backdated to 1 July 2024, it also affects 2024-25 returns (amendments), which the page does not mention.

claims: employer, bank and health insurer data typically flows through automatically by late July
whys: The writer's rewrite now has the ATO as subject ('The ATO prefills a large part of your return'). The prefill timing ('by late July') is uncited, and the 'typically' hedge was already in the original. Confirm against the ATO prefill availability page for 2026.

whys: Concessional and non-concessional caps are indexed to AWOTE separately from the transfer balance cap. Only the total super balance thresholds (and bring-forward thresholds) are tied to the general TBC, so 'links directly' overstates the link.

claims: Rates run from 4% (Tasmania's first band) to 8.75% (ACT, above $150 million)
